verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration stating the product for an arbitrary pair of derivative multi-indices I, J was found. Lean states the undifferentiated cross-label vanishing: `supported_cross_product_zero` gives u_l(x,θ)_i · v_k(x,θ)_j = 0 whenever label n l ≠ label n k (level ≥ 1), from disjoint slot supports, and `supported_product_germ` upgrades it to vanishing on a whole neighbourhood. Derivatives enter only where the fields are used: `supported_transport_zero` (via `transport_zero_of_product_germ`) kills cross-label advection, but the cylindrical transport operator differentiates the right factor only, so the case I ≠ 0 and J ≠ 0 simultaneously is never stated. The paper's form does follow from the germ form for smooth fields: {u ≠ 0} is open and v ≡ 0 there, so at a point x either a neighbourhood has u ≡ 0, whence ∂^I u(x) = 0, or x lies in the closure of an open set on which v ≡ 0, whence ∂^J v(x) = 0 by continuity of the derivatives; with the disjoint-tsupport hypothesis of `zero_germ_of_disjoint_on` this is a two-line argument. Rated low because the cross-label cancellation the paper draws from this line is what the Lean proves, by the germ route.
